Thanks — looping in implementation and infra owners so we can align on a practical sprint plan. Below is the initial enablement checklist I’ll use to drive the first two sprints. I’ve attached the checklist as a simple markdown stub too.

Sprint 0 (prep, 3–5 business days)
- Confirm PO + billing contact (Procurement) — owner: Aditya / Liam
- Decide primary region (we recommend us-west1 given latency to your users) — owner: Greenfield
- Netops info: project id, VPC CIDR, peering window & contact — owner: Priya Shah / priprocure@greenfieldhealth.com
- KMS & key access model (Customer-managed key preferred for Private) — owner: Greenfield infra
- Security docs: SOC2, SC-tenant config review — owner: Redwood Security / Greenfield

Sprint 1 (provisioning, 5–8 business days)
- Provision reserved GPU pool (8 x A100 equiv.) and attach to VPC peering
- Configure autoscale policy: baseline nodes, burst caps, cooldowns — owner: Karthik
- Model pinning / container images to be approved — owner: Marissa + Greenfield ML
- Test inference workflows against staging endpoints

Sprint 2 (cutover & go-live prep, 3–5 business days)
- Dry-run failover to fallback region (us-east4)
- Cost guardrails and alerting configured in Console
- Runbook handoff to Greenfield ops + knowledge transfer session

Open questions for the kickoff:
- Confirm expected peak concurrency and acceptable cold-start latency
- Any restricted IP ranges or egress policies beyond standard peering?

Subject: Re: Greenfield Health — internal provisioning notes

Internal notes / infra profile for this customer (to bring to the kickoff):
- Requested pool: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent), TF32 and FP16 workloads expected
- Autoscale profile (recommended initial):
  - min_nodes: 2
  - scale_target_utilization: 60% (average token generation cpu/gpu utilization target)
  - burst_limit_nodes: 12 (hard cap for scheduled campaigns)
  - cooldown_window: 180s
  - scale_up_policy: fast (immediate up to burst ceiling), scale_down: gradual
- Batching config: default dynamic batching, target batch latency 80ms
- Regional choice: primary us-west1 (low latency to their east-coast users via CDN), fallback us-east4
- Observability: token-level billing enabled, per-route latency SLOs

Netops asks to confirm with customer:
- Do they want burst capacity billed as on-demand overage or scheduled reserved bursts?
- Will they provide a list of CIDRs for egress allowlist?

I’ll prepare a short runbook snippet and a playbook for peering and KMS steps.

—Monica
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
